title: Audit Console: reliable query, cursor export, and sharable saved-queries
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
Redwood's console audit viewer is the canonical place admins investigate account activity. With RBAC v2 rolling out and more customers using SSO/SAML, we need exports and saved queries that are reliable, reproducible, and respect org-level permissions. Current issues: large result sets time out, CSV exports corrupt multiline messages, saved queries can't be shared across teams, and incremental re-exports are brittle under pagination changes.

Objective:
Deliver a robust audit console experience that supports: streaming CSV/JSON export for large result sets, opaque cursor-based pagination for consistent incremental exports, advanced filter semantics (time-range, actor, resource, action, region, model, route), and saved-query sharing with RBAC controls. Exports must preserve UTF-8/CSV escaping, include metadata (cursor token, query fingerprint), and be resumable from last acked cursor.

Scope:
- Console: UI to build, run, save, and share queries; export buttons (CSV/JSON) with progress and resumability.
- Backend: query planner endpoint that returns stable cursors and stateless export tokens; streaming export job that produces newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) and CSV with proper escaping.
- RBAC v2: saved-query visibility rules and export permission checks; SAML groups map to console RBAC.
- Observability: export metrics (bytes, rows, duration), failure reasons, and audit events for export initiation/completion.

Out of scope:
- Reindexing historical raw logs (handled by infra tickets).
- New long-term archival UI (separate product work).

Acceptance criteria (high level):
1) Large exports (>5M rows) complete without client timeouts via server-side streaming and resumable cursors.
2) CSV exporter correctly escapes multi-line messages, embedded commas, and unicode; verified by unit+integration tests.
3) Saved queries can be shared with roles/groups created via RBAC v2 and honor SSO/SAML group membership.
4) Incremental export uses opaque cursor tokens that are stable across retries and include a fingerprint to detect schema drift.
5) Console shows export job status, bytes written, rows exported, and provides download link when ready.
6) All export actions are recorded in audit logs with actor, query_id, export_format, and success/failure reason.

Implementation notes / tradeoffs:
- Cursor model: use a server-generated opaque token containing the shard id + last-offset + signature. This avoids leaking internal offsets and allows backend to verify token freshness. Tradeoff: tokens need rotation handling for deployments where the index topology changes; plan is to include a token version and fallback to a full query scan when token invalid.
- Streaming vs chunked files: streaming NDJSON is best for JSON consumers; CSV will be streamed as bytes with consistent headers. For large downloads we'll stage files in object storage for clients that need random access or HTTP-range.
- Pagination semantics: Elastic-style search_after is unstable for concurrent writes; prefer stable composite-key pagination or backed cursor anchored to immutable ingestion sequence for export jobs. This will be implemented behind a query planner service.
- RBAC checks: evaluate both at query creation time (saved-query visibility) and export time (to prevent elevation by reusing someone else's query).

API sketch (for implementers):
- POST /v2/internal/audit/query-plan -> {query, filters} returns {plan_id, first_cursor_token} (short-lived)
- POST /v2/internal/audit/export?format=csv|json -> {plan_id, cursor_token} returns 202 + job_id
- GET /v2/internal/audit/export/{job_id}/status -> {state, bytes, rows, download_url}
- POST /v2/internal/audit/export/{job_id}/resume -> {cursor_token}

(These internal endpoints will be wrapped by console-facing endpoints that perform RBAC checks and return user-friendly errors.)

Testing & QA:
- Unit tests for CSV escaping across 50+ edge cases (quotes, newlines, emojis, long fields).
- Load tests simulating 10 concurrent 5M-row exports to validate memory usage and throughput.
- Security tests to ensure saved-query sharing respects RBAC groups, and SAML group syncs produce expected visibility.
- Integration test to verify cursor resume after simulated topology change returns safe fallback or detectable error code.

Rollout plan:
1) Backend query planner + streaming export (feature-flag) internal-only.
2) Console UI for saved queries + simple exports to small datasets, enable to a subset of orgs.
3) Gradual enablement for large exports and saved-query sharing across teams.

Memory usage looks stable for 1M row exports but we need to validate object storage staging for >5M. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4128

2025-02-18 — Priya Shah (Security Review): noted we must include exporter audit events and ensure tokens are signed with rotating KMS keys. Marked security_review_required; started checklist in Confluence.

2025-02-20 — UX (Ben Carter): initial saved-query sharing mockups uploaded. We prefer role-based share options (Team / Organization / Private). Link: https://go.redwood/drive/design/audit-saved-queries
2025-02-24 — QA (Daniel Kim): found CSV escaping regression for CRLF inside message field; added failing test. Putting a small blocker on CSV until patch applied.
2025-02-27 — Marco Liu: patched CSV writer to always use "" quoting and escape quotes by doubling. Added integration test suite. Re-ran load tests, preliminary pass at 5M rows with staged S3 uploads.
